subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In screen printing, areas you do not want printed are blocked using a...
questions.explain: A stencil on the mesh blocks the ink so it only passes through the open, unblocked areas.

questions.q: A 'storyboard' is most useful for planning...
options: A sequence such as an animation or advert
questions.explain: A storyboard sketches a sequence of frames to plan how an animation or film will unfold.

questions.q: What term describes a range of related colours that sit next to each other on the colour wheel?
questions.explain: Analogous or harmonious colours sit beside each other on the wheel and blend smoothly.

questions.q: Why is knowing the 'target audience' important in a design?
options: It decides the price of paint
It shapes style, tone and content to suit who the design is for
It is only needed for sculpture
It has no effect on the design
questions.explain: Understanding the target audience guides the style, language and imagery so the design appeals to them.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: Corrugated card is useful in 3D work because it is...
options: Lightweight, strong and easy to score and fold
questions.explain: Corrugated card is light yet rigid, and can be scored and folded to build 3D forms.

questions.q: 'Product design' is the discipline of...
options: Designing functional objects people use, such as appliances and furniture
questions.explain: Product design develops functional, manufactured objects, balancing how they work and look.

questions.q: Which set lists the three primary colours?
questions.explain: In traditional art theory the primaries are red, yellow and blue, from which other colours are mixed.

questions.q: Weaving creates fabric by...
options: Looping a single yarn with needles
Interlacing warp and weft threads at right angles
questions.explain: Weaving interlaces vertical warp threads with horizontal weft threads to make cloth.

questions.q: In 3D design, a 'maquette' or model is made to...
options: Test and plan ideas before making the final piece
questions.explain: A model or maquette lets a designer test scale, form and ideas before committing to the final work.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: Throwing is a ceramics technique that uses...
options: A potter's wheel to shape clay
questions.explain: Throwing shapes clay into rounded forms by hand as it spins on a potter's wheel.

questions.q: 'Surface decoration' in textiles refers to...
options: Patterns or marks added onto the surface of a fabric
The fibre the fabric is made from
The way the cloth is woven
questions.explain: Surface decoration covers techniques such as printing, embroidery or dyeing applied to a fabric's surface.

questions.q: What is cross-hatching?
options: Two sets of parallel lines crossing to build darker tone
Dotting the surface to suggest tone
questions.explain: Cross-hatching layers a second set of lines across the first to create darker, denser tone.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing blue and yellow?
questions.explain: Blue mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour green.

questions.q: 'Devore' (burnout) is a technique that...
options: Uses a chemical to dissolve fibres and leave a sheer pattern
questions.explain: Devore applies a chemical paste that burns away certain fibres, leaving a sheer patterned effect.

questions.q: A 'wordmark' (logotype) is a logo made from...
options: A stylised version of the brand's name in text
questions.explain: A wordmark is a logo formed from the company name set in distinctive, designed lettering.

questions.q: Which photographer is famous for dramatic black-and-white landscapes of the American West, such as Yosemite?
questions.explain: Ansel Adams is renowned for his sharp, high-contrast black-and-white landscape photographs.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: Crochet creates fabric using...
options: A single hooked needle to interlock loops
questions.explain: Crochet uses one hooked needle to pull yarn through loops, building up the fabric.

questions.q: What does ISO measure on a camera?
questions.explain: ISO sets the sensor's sensitivity to light; a high ISO brightens images but can add noise.

questions.q: Appliqué is a technique that involves...
options: Stitching shaped pieces of fabric onto a larger background cloth
questions.explain: Appliqué sews cut pieces of fabric onto a background to build up an image or pattern.
